paper.title: Algorithm 684: C1 and C2 interpolation on triangles with quintic and nonic bivariate polynomials
paper.note: DOI not verified in this wake; the article itself was not read, so the claim rests on the value the shipped program prints as its expected value.

code.note: A single Fortran file: the algorithm subroutines plus PROGRAM DFC1C2, an example driver written by the author (A. Preusser, 1989). Compile the whole file with a Fortran 77 compiler and run the program.

claim.location: The driver PROGRAM DFC1C2 in 684.gz (source lines 105-106 and again 144-145): WRITE (*,999) 3.035646151154D0, Z(44,03) prints 'EXPECTED VALUE' 3.035646151154 next to the COMPUTED VALUE of Z(44,3) on the rectangular grid built from the example's scattered data. The author's own comment says the default single-precision build can lose up to three digits.

reference.file: 684.gz member: PROGRAM DFC1C2, the expected value constant in the WRITE statement

claim.metric: Z(44,3) computed by the example driver, compared with the author's expected constant 3.035646151154.
claim.paper_value: Not used: the TOMS article was not read in this wake; the value is the expected constant written into the shipped driver.

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The shipped comment states that up to three digits can be lost in the default single-precision computation, and the expected constant is printed to 12 decimals. A tolerance of 1e-3 absolute accepts that known single-precision loss and still rejects a wrong interpolant. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 2 minutes: one Fortran compile and one run of the example.
cost.data_size: None (the scattered data are inside the driver).
cost.data_licence: Netlib TOMS code under the ACM licence; the rerun should record the licence text.

why: A deterministic interpolation code whose author ships an expected value for one computed grid value, so the claim tests whether the C1/C2 polynomial construction still reproduces it.
